title: Sector
summary: Top-level business definitions and decision guidance for deciding the broadest classification.

definitions.label: Real Estate
definitions.description:
The company's primary business is owning, operating, transacting, financing, or servicing property assets. Real property is central to what the company is, not just one exposure among many.


a
notes: Use this when property is clearly the business model.
Do not use this when real estate is just one exposure inside a broader capital or service platform.

definitions.label: Financial Services
definitions.description: The company's primary business is deploying, advising on, underwriting, trading, structuring, or servicing capital and financial products. Real estate may appear in the portfolio, but property is not the main operating identity.
notes: Use this when the firm feels capital-led rather than property-led.
Family office language is not enough on its own; look for what the capital is actually being deployed into.

definitions.label: Recruiting
definitions.description: The company's primary business is talent placement, executive search, recruiting process support, or staffing. The sector may still specialize by end market, but the business model is recruiting.
notes: Treat end-market specialization as a downstream clue, not the top-level sector.
A real estate company hiring aggressively is still Real Estate, not Recruiting.

definitions.label: Other
definitions.description: The company does not fit one of the primary marketed sectors with enough confidence, or the available evidence is too weak or too mixed to place it cleanly elsewhere.
examples: Generic holding companies with weak evidence
notes: This is a fallback, not a target state.
Return it with an explicit reason when the available evidence is genuinely weak or conflicting.

rules.name: Start With The Primary Business Model
rules.directive: Before you look at isolated keywords, decide whether the company primarily makes money by owning property, deploying capital, or placing talent. Use that operating model as the first sector decision.
rules.why: This reduces false positives created by websites that mention many adjacent services or markets.
examples: "We acquire and operate" points toward Real Estate.
"We invest across credit and equity strategies" points toward Financial Services.
rules.stopCondition: If the company's business model is explicit and consistent across multiple fields, stop sector analysis.

rules.name: Favor Property-Led Identity Over Loose Real Estate Exposure
rules.directive: Do not classify a company as Real Estate just because it mentions property, lenders, or portfolio exposure. Choose Real Estate only when property is central to what the company actually is.
rules.why: Many finance, legal, and recruiting firms use real-estate-heavy language without being real estate companies.
examples: A credit fund with a real estate sleeve can still be Financial Services.
A law firm serving developers is not Real Estate.

rules.name: Use Entity Separation As An Override
rules.directive: When the company JSON represents a distinct legal or branded entity, classify that entity on its own merits even if the parent group operates in another sector.
rules.why: The business wants each marketed entity classified on what it actually is.
examples: A recruiting affiliate inside an investment platform can still be Recruiting.
A capital markets subsidiary can still be Financial Services even if the parent touches property.

rules.name: Let Leadership Titles Break Ties
rules.directive: If the website copy is broad or fuzzy, use the subset of people and titles to infer the operating center of gravity. Investment titles support capital-led models, brokerage titles support service-led real estate, and search titles support recruiting.
rules.why: Titles often clarify the business model when marketing copy is vague.
examples: A team dominated by acquisitions and asset-management roles supports Real Estate.
A team dominated by recruiters and talent-partner titles supports Recruiting.

rules.name: Return Best Guess With Confidence
rules.directive: Always return a sector, even when evidence is incomplete. Lower the confidence score and explain the missing or conflicting evidence instead of refusing to classify.
rules.why: The product decision is to prefer best guesses with confidence over blanks.
examples: "Best guess: Financial Services because debt and capital-markets language dominates, but confidence is 2/5 because property language is also present."

title: Vertical
summary: Primary operating identities inside each sector, with the guidance for deciding which one wins.

definitions.label: Real Estate Investment Company
definitions.description: A principal business that owns, acquires, develops, or operates property on its own balance sheet or on behalf of an investment vehicle. The company is acting as owner or sponsor rather than agent.
notes: Signals include acquisitions, asset management, portfolio ownership, capital deployment, and development under ownership.

definitions.label: Real Estate Services
definitions.description: A service-led real estate business that represents clients, manages assets for others, advises on transactions, or provides operating support without being the principal owner of the underlying properties.
notes: The key distinction is agency or client service rather than principal ownership.

definitions.label: Real Estate Finance
definitions.description: A real estate-focused capital provider or finance platform. The firm lends against property, structures debt, or operates primarily on the financing side of the asset rather than the ownership or brokerage side.
notes: Use this when the company's core identity is lending or structured real estate finance.

definitions.label: Financial Services Platform
definitions.description: A finance-led company whose clearest identity is investing, advising, underwriting, structuring, or managing financial products rather than property or recruiting services.
notes: This is a starter vertical until the finance playbook expands.

definitions.label: Recruiting Firm
definitions.description: A company primarily engaged in search, staffing, or placement. Sector specialization should be reflected in keywords and email industry, not by changing the core vertical away from recruiting.
notes: Use specialization clues such as real estate or finance downstream.

definitions.label: Other / Unclear
definitions.description: A fallback vertical when the company cannot be cleanly placed from the available evidence, or when the sector is weakly supported and no specific operating model stands out.
notes: Return with low confidence and explain what evidence was missing.

rules.name: Inside Real Estate, Decide Principal vs Service vs Lender
rules.directive: If the sector is Real Estate, determine whether the company is primarily a principal owner or investor, a service or advisory firm, or a finance platform. This distinction should drive the vertical more than asset-class keywords.
rules.why: This is the core structural distinction in the guidebook.
examples: "Own, acquire, and develop" points to Real Estate Investment Company.
"Tenant representation" points to Real Estate Services.
"Bridge lending" points to Real Estate Finance.
rules.stopCondition: If principal, service, or lender identity is explicit, stop further vertical debate.

rules.name: Choose One Primary Vertical Even If Multiple Are Plausible
rules.directive: Return one winning vertical. You may mention alternatives in the reason, but the visible output should still have one primary answer.
rules.why: The product direction is that users expect one vertical to win in the wash.
examples: A brokerage-investment hybrid can still resolve to Real Estate Services if agency work is the dominant public identity.

rules.name: Use Titles To Resolve Fuzzy Marketing Copy
rules.directive: When the homepage is generic, inspect leadership titles and personnel clues. Acquisitions, investments, and asset management lean principal; brokers and tenant reps lean services; lending and originations lean finance; search titles lean recruiting.
rules.why: The product will deliberately send person name and title subsets for this purpose.
examples: A firm with generic copy but multiple Managing Directors of Originations should resolve to Real Estate Finance.

rules.name: Keep Vertical Consistent With The Sector Decision
rules.directive: Do not let a single keyword drag the company into an incompatible vertical. Once the sector is decided, choose from the verticals that actually fit that sector unless the sector itself should be reconsidered.
rules.why: This keeps the hierarchy coherent and easier for users to understand.
examples: A finance-led company mentioning acquisitions should still resolve to a finance-oriented vertical if ownership evidence is weak.

title: Keywords
summary: Business phrases used as evidence, output, and user-facing explanation, including what gets shown versus held internally.

definitions.label: Acquisitions
definitions.description: Signals buying, sourcing, or underwriting assets, businesses, or portfolios.
notes: Strong support for principal investment models when paired with ownership language.

definitions.label: Asset Management
definitions.description: Signals active management of owned or invested assets to improve returns, occupancy, operations, or performance.
notes: Often supports Real Estate Investment or Financial Services depending on the rest of the context.

definitions.label: Bridge Loan
definitions.description: Signals short-term real estate lending or transitional financing.
notes: Strong signal toward Real Estate Finance.

definitions.label: Commercial Brokerage
definitions.description: Signals brokerage activity representing landlords, tenants, buyers, or sellers in commercial property.
notes: Strong signal toward Real Estate Services or Big Brokerage email industry.

definitions.label: Development
definitions.description: Signals creating or materially repositioning property or platforms from planning through execution.
notes: Can support Real Estate Investment or broader finance-led ownership strategies depending on who owns the risk.

definitions.label: Family Office
definitions.description: Signals capital managed on behalf of one or more families, often with long hold periods and flexible mandates.
notes: Treat carefully. It becomes stronger when paired with clear asset-class language.

definitions.label: Multi-Family
definitions.description: Signals apartments or housing assets with multiple units.
notes: Useful for RE Residential, PE RE, and visible keyword output.

definitions.label: Private Credit
definitions.description: Signals private lending, debt investing, or credit-focused capital strategies.
notes: Often supports Financial Services or Real Estate Finance.

definitions.label: PropTech
definitions.description: Signals software, data, or technology products serving the property ecosystem.
notes: May support Real Estate Services, Services, or Prop Tech-style email industries depending on the company model.

definitions.label: 3rd Party Property Management
definitions.description: Signals management of buildings on behalf of clients rather than management of the company's own portfolio.
notes: Explicitly distinguish from owner-led in-house property management.

definitions.label: REIT
definitions.description: Signals a publicly traded or private real estate investment trust structure owning, financing, or operating income-producing property.

definitions.label: Private Equity
definitions.description: Signals sponsor-led private equity capital pursuing control, platform building, or value creation investments.

definitions.label: Institutional
definitions.description: Signals an institutional-grade investment, ownership, or client profile tied to pensions, endowments, sovereign capital, or large asset managers.

definitions.label: Leasing
definitions.description: Signals a leasing-focused business line involving tenanting, occupancy growth, or representation around lease transactions.

definitions.label: Transactions
definitions.description: Signals deal execution work around purchases, sales, financings, recapitalizations, or other transaction events.

definitions.label: Investment Management
definitions.description: Signals discretionary or advisory management of investment portfolios, funds, or capital programs.

definitions.label: Property Management
definitions.description: Signals day-to-day building or portfolio operations, tenant service, maintenance oversight, and performance management.

definitions.label: Hospitality
definitions.description: Signals a hospitality operating or investing focus centered on lodging, guest experience, or hotel-like real estate.

definitions.label: Hotels
definitions.description: Signals ownership, operation, development, brokerage, or financing tied specifically to hotel assets.

definitions.label: Resorts
definitions.description: Signals ownership, operation, development, or financing tied specifically to resort assets and destinations.

definitions.label: Vacation Rentals
definitions.description: Signals short-term rental inventory, management, software, brokerage, or investment tied to vacation stays.

definitions.label: Affordable Housing
definitions.description: Signals affordable housing ownership, development, preservation, financing, or services.

definitions.label: Workforce Housing
definitions.description: Signals workforce housing ownership, development, financing, or services aimed at middle-income renters.

definitions.label: Self-Storage
definitions.description: Signals ownership, operation, brokerage, financing, or technology tied to self-storage facilities.

definitions.label: Data Centers
definitions.description: Signals ownership, development, operation, financing, or services tied to data center real estate.

definitions.label: Senior Housing
definitions.description: Signals ownership, operation, development, or financing tied to senior living or age-restricted housing.

definitions.label: ESG
definitions.description: Signals environmental, social, and governance positioning, sustainability priorities, or impact-oriented operating language.

definitions.label: Single-Family
definitions.description: Signals single-family housing, rental homes, build-for-rent communities, or related investment activity.

definitions.label: Industrial
definitions.description: Signals industrial property such as warehouses, logistics facilities, flex, or light manufacturing space.

definitions.label: Office
definitions.description: Signals office property ownership, leasing, development, financing, or workplace-oriented services.

definitions.label: Land
definitions.description: Signals land ownership, entitlement, development, brokerage, or financing before vertical improvements.

definitions.label: Manufactured Homes
definitions.description: Signals manufactured housing communities, modular housing, or related investment and operations.

definitions.label: Medical Office
definitions.description: Signals medical office buildings, outpatient facilities, or healthcare-oriented office real estate.

definitions.label: Mixed-Use
definitions.description: Signals assets or developments combining multiple uses such as residential, retail, office, or hospitality.

definitions.label: Residential
definitions.description: Signals housing-oriented ownership, operation, development, financing, or services across living asset types.

definitions.label: Commercial
definitions.description: Signals non-residential property or business activity centered on income-producing commercial real estate.

definitions.label: Investment Advisory
definitions.description: Signals investment advice, capital placement, portfolio guidance, or strategic recommendations to investors.

definitions.label: Capital Markets
definitions.description: Signals capital raising, debt placement, structured finance, or markets execution around investment transactions.

definitions.label: Investment Services
definitions.description: Signals investor-facing services supporting capital allocation, execution, reporting, or portfolio administration.

definitions.label: Tenant Representation
definitions.description: Signals tenant-side advisory or brokerage work for occupiers in site selection, negotiation, or workplace strategy.

definitions.label: Landlord Representation
definitions.description: Signals owner-side leasing or advisory work representing landlords in marketing and negotiation.

definitions.label: Auctions
definitions.description: Signals auction-based disposition, bidding, or sale execution for assets, property, or portfolios.

definitions.label: Automation
definitions.description: Signals automation of workflows, operations, or repetitive tasks through software, systems, or robotics.

definitions.label: Analytics
definitions.description: Signals data analysis, benchmarking, forecasting, or decision support as a core offering or differentiator.

definitions.label: Predictive AI
definitions.description: Signals predictive AI, machine learning, or modeled forecasting used to improve decisions or operations.

definitions.label: Digital Tools
definitions.description: Signals software tools, digital workflows, or online platforms used to power a business line or product.

definitions.label: Mortgage REIT
definitions.description: Signals a mortgage REIT strategy focused on mortgage-backed assets, real estate debt, or interest income.

definitions.label: Debt Financing
definitions.description: Signals debt capital provision, debt placement, or financing structures centered on borrowing.

definitions.label: Investment Structuring
definitions.description: Signals legal, tax, or capital structuring work shaping how investments or deals are organized.

definitions.label: CMBS
definitions.description: Signals commercial mortgage-backed securities activity, products, or investment focus.

definitions.label: RMBS
definitions.description: Signals residential mortgage-backed securities activity, products, or investment focus.

definitions.label: MBS
definitions.description: Signals mortgage-backed securities activity, products, or investment focus more generally.

definitions.label: Loans
definitions.description: Signals loan origination, underwriting, servicing, brokering, or investing as a core activity.

definitions.label: Financing
definitions.description: Signals financing solutions, capital sourcing, or funding support without limiting to one specific instrument.

definitions.label: Mortgage
definitions.description: Signals mortgage lending, servicing, brokerage, banking, or mortgage-focused investing.

definitions.label: Real Estate Investments
definitions.description: Signals a broad real estate investment mandate spanning acquisitions, ownership, asset management, or portfolio building.

definitions.label: Wealth Advisory
definitions.description: Signals advisory work for high-net-worth clients on wealth planning, asset allocation, or portfolio strategy.

definitions.label: Private Banking
definitions.description: Signals bank-led wealth, lending, and relationship services for affluent or ultra-high-net-worth clients.

definitions.label: Alternative Investing
definitions.description: Signals alternatives such as private markets, hedge funds, real assets, or non-traditional strategies.

definitions.label: Hedge Funds
definitions.description: Signals hedge fund management, hedge fund investing, or related capital allocation services.

definitions.label: Retirement Services
definitions.description: Signals retirement planning, retirement administration, or retirement-focused advisory services.

definitions.label: 401k
definitions.description: Signals 401(k) plan administration, advisory, recordkeeping, or retirement benefits support.

definitions.label: Annuities
definitions.description: Signals annuity products, annuity advisory, or insurance-linked retirement income solutions.

definitions.label: Stocks
definitions.description: Signals public equity investing, trading, research, or brokerage tied to stocks.

definitions.label: Bonds
definitions.description: Signals fixed-income investing, trading, advisory, or research tied to bonds.

definitions.label: ETFs
definitions.description: Signals exchange-traded fund products, investing, trading, or advisory services.

definitions.label: Blockchain
definitions.description: Signals blockchain infrastructure, products, or strategy as a meaningful part of the business model.

definitions.label: Cryptocurrency
definitions.description: Signals cryptocurrency investing, trading, infrastructure, payments, or treasury exposure.

definitions.label: DeFi
definitions.description: Signals decentralized finance products, protocols, investing, or infrastructure.

definitions.label: Digital-Only Banking
definitions.description: Signals banking products delivered without traditional branch infrastructure through digital-first channels.

definitions.label: Payment Systems
definitions.description: Signals payments infrastructure, money movement, merchant processing, or transaction rails.

definitions.label: Credit Rating
definitions.description: Signals credit ratings, credit analysis, or risk-scoring products and services.

definitions.label: Fraud Prevention
definitions.description: Signals fraud detection, fraud prevention, or trust-and-safety controls around financial activity.

definitions.label: AML
definitions.description: Signals anti-money laundering controls, compliance operations, or regulatory screening.

definitions.label: Retail
definitions.description: Signals retail property, retail tenants, shopping centers, or consumer-facing commerce environments.

definitions.label: VC
definitions.description: Signals venture capital investing, startup backing, or early-stage portfolio management.

rules.name: Use Keywords As Evidence, Not As The Whole Decision
rules.directive: Keywords should support the larger company interpretation. Do not let one isolated phrase outweigh an obviously different business model unless the phrase is highly specific.
rules.why: A fuzzy website can mention many adjacent concepts without actually being that kind of company.
examples: "Development" alone is not enough to force Real Estate Investment if everything else points elsewhere.

rules.name: Visible Keywords Must Be A Subset Of All Keywords
rules.directive: Only show keywords that were actually detected or inferred with support. Never invent a visible keyword that is not represented somewhere in the underlying evidence set.
rules.why: Visible Keywords must be explainable back to All Keywords.
signals: Inferred keywords with strong textual support
examples: If All Keywords includes Multi-Family and Acquisitions, Visible Keywords can show one or both if they are confidence-worthy.

rules.name: Prefer Specific Business Phrases Over Generic Context
rules.directive: Choose visible keywords that tell a human what kind of company this is, not merely what broad market it touches. Avoid showing weak context words when stronger phrases are available.
rules.why: The output should read like a useful explanation, not matcher debris.
examples: Show Bridge Loan instead of just Financing.
Show Commercial Brokerage instead of just Transactions.

rules.name: Order Visible Keywords By Confidence And Explanatory Value
rules.directive: Sort visible keywords from strongest and most explanatory to weakest. Do not overload the surface with low-confidence extras if the top few already explain the result.
rules.why: A short clean list is more useful than a noisy wall of tags.
examples: For a PE real estate firm, Private Equity, Acquisitions, and Multi-Family may be enough even if many weaker keywords also matched.

rules.name: Call Out When The Top Keywords Were Enough
rules.directive: If you intentionally stopped adding visible keywords because the top terms already explain the classification, say that in the reason text.
rules.why: The team wants stop-language reflected back in plain English.
examples: "We stopped after the top three visible keywords because they already explained the winning profile."

title: Email Industry
summary: Current downstream campaign buckets and the guidance for translating richer classification into those familiar labels.

definitions.label: PE RE
definitions.description: Real estate investment groups whose identity is private-equity-style capital deployment into property assets.

definitions.label: RE Commercial
definitions.description: Commercial real estate owners, operators, developers, or service providers not better captured by a narrower override.

definitions.label: RE Residential
definitions.description: Residential real estate companies focused on apartments, single-family rentals, home communities, or other housing-centric asset types.

definitions.label: RE Finance
definitions.description: Real estate lenders and finance platforms whose identity is debt, structured finance, or capital provision into property.

definitions.label: Big Brokerage
definitions.description: Large-scale brokerage and transaction-oriented real estate service organizations.

definitions.label: Financial
definitions.description: General financial-services firms when a more specific real-estate or recruiting bucket does not apply.

definitions.label: RE Recruiters
definitions.description: Recruiting firms whose clearest end-market specialization is real estate.

definitions.label: Recruiters Financial
definitions.description: Recruiting firms whose clearest end-market specialization is financial services.

definitions.label: Services
definitions.description: A broad services fallback for business models that are service-led but not cleanly mapped to a narrower current bucket.

definitions.label: Other
definitions.description: Final fallback when nothing more specific is defensible.

rules.name: Translate After Sector And Vertical Are Stable
rules.directive: Do not guess Email Industry from keywords alone. First decide sector and vertical, then use keywords to refine the translation into an existing email-industry bucket.
rules.why: The same keyword can mean different things depending on whether the company is principal, service-led, or finance-led.
examples: Private Equity plus Real Estate cues should translate toward PE RE, not generic Financial.

rules.name: Favor Existing CRM Buckets
rules.directive: Use the current recognizable CRM bucket names when the choice is close. Preserve continuity for reporting, campaigns, and human expectations.
rules.why: This keeps the system aligned with downstream operational workflows.
examples: Commercial brokerage should map to Big Brokerage rather than inventing a new brokerage bucket.

rules.name: Apply Specific Overrides Before Broad Fallbacks
rules.directive: Apply specific overrides such as Family Office, RE Finance, RE Recruiters, or Recruiters Financial before falling back to broad labels like RE Commercial, Financial, Services, or Other.
rules.why: Specific buckets are more useful when the evidence supports them.
examples: A recruiter focused on financial services should land in Recruiters Financial, not generic Recruiting or Financial.
rules.stopCondition: If a clear specific override applies, stop translation there.

rules.name: Use Other Only As A True Last Resort
rules.directive: Choose Other only when no stable current bucket is defensible. If you land on Other, explain exactly what evidence was missing or too mixed.
rules.why: Other is operationally necessary but low-value unless the reasoning is explicit.
examples: A generic holding page with thin evidence can return Other at 1/5 confidence.
